iti62:1.1: These three faculties—found at [dn33:1.10.111]() and [sn48.23:1.3]()—are indicative of a growing fascination with analyzing the details of what exactly happens in the process of enlightenment. The exact meaning is not obvious, but the verses here offer clues to interpretation, so I annotate them closely.
iti62:2.1: The three faculties are mentioned in late canonical texts, which treat them as starting with stream-entry, whereas I believe, based on the terms themselves and the verses, that they concern the realization of arahantship. Briefly, the Abhidhamma Vibhaṅga, albeit cryptically, indicates that the first two faculties are the path to stream-entry and the practice of the trainee from stream-entry onward ([vb5:24.1]()). Later texts are more explicit. The Nettipakaraṇa says the first faculty leads to overcoming the first three fetters, i.e. stream-entry ([ne5:28.1]()). This is consistent with [ne37:392.1]() and the Peṭakopadesa at [pe3:35.1](), which explain this faculty as the effort to realize the four noble truths for the first time. Even more explicit is the Paṭisambhidāmagga at [ps1.4:91.1]() = [ps1.1:513.1](), which says the first faculty occurs at “the moment of the path to stream-entry”. The idea of the “path moment”, however, is alien to the Suttas, and indicates a substantial period of doctrinal development; these texts were all written long after the Buddha. The commentary builds on these explanation, for which see Bodhi’s note in *Connected Discourses* on [sn48.23](). Despite this impressive consistency, the verses here say nothing about stream-entry, and from the first speak solely about arahantship.
iti62:2.3: The key term is _aññā_ (“enlightenment”), which is used throughout the Suttas to indicate the realization of arahantship specifically. The later texts take it as a synonym for the knowledge or realization of a stream-enterer. This is linguistically possible, but not supported by usage in the Suttas. | “The faculty of understanding that one’s enlightenment is imminent” is literally, “The faculty aware that ‘I shall know the unknown’”.
iti62:2.6: Now follow three verses, which correlate one-by-one to the three faculties, and constitute the earliest explanation of the three faculties. In brief, I think the three faculties apply to: (1) one on the path to arahantship; (2) one on the occasion of realizing arahantship; (3) one living as an arahant.
iti62:3.1: This first line indicates that the first faculty is restricted to those who have entered the noble path. The commentary takes this as meaning *all* those who have entered the noble path, but I think it is a subset, namely the one “practicing to realize the fruit of arahantship”. This is a person, not a mind moment ([mn142:5.9]()).
iti62:3.3: In the Suttas, this is normally the “knowledge of the ending of defilements”, which is characteristic of the arahant (eg. [sn12.23]()).
iti62:3.4: Ending of defilements “without delay” (_anantarā_) is taught numerous time as the advanced meditation practice aimed squarely at arahantship in this very life, typically explained as seeing the impermanence of the five aggregates ([sn22.55:10.1](), [sn22.81:5.1](), [an5.170](), [an6.27](), [an6.28]()). Also similar is the stock phrase “enlightenment in this very life” (_diṭṭheva dhamme aññā_, [sn47.36:1.9]()). This seems to exclude most of those on the noble path: even the non-returners can expect one more life. Only the seventh of the eight noble individuals, those who have entered the path to arahantship, are assured of enlightenment in this very life. Taken with the previous line, this indicates that those on the path to arahantship first see that the defilements are ending, then (as the next faculty) realize arahantship itself (see [dn34:1.3.25]()). In fact, it would seems as if the point of these three faculties is to clarify this process.
iti62:4.4: The second faculty comes immediately after defilements have ended, when the new arahant reflects on their experience and understands that they are no longer trapped in the cycle of rebirth.
iti62:5.4: The final faculty is the arahant living out their last life in peace.
